items.title: Ran Blake interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 16, 2021
items.q: But as it was I had so many people like Jason Rogers helping me and so many others.

ctx.x: Yes. Recently I had a conversation with a friend that I’ve had an almost 50-year friendship, a fellow musician, and maybe because we had some of that same brandy that you had on the plane, but we were getting sort of reminiscing about our careers and we got into the what are we leaving behind? Have we made any contributions that will outlive us? And so I guess I’m wondering, have you thought about your legacy? What do you hope will be Ran Blake’s lasting contribution?

I love a couple of — more than a couple, I love my music to be performed by others, but I think my legacy is the book. It could be longer, I could revitalize it with experiences. But as it was I had so many people like Jason Rogers helping me and so many others. I think that the ears should be used more. Now this is not my invention, in India, Africa, from grandmother to grandson, this tradition has been around us and it may have been through the beginning of Duke Ellington when starting his band in Washington.…
You’re a poet also, Ran. Thank you for that.
